edit.description: the win32-only `pinLongPaths` block (:1861) is the only one reaching `getLocalConfig`; the sibling pin it reaches parity with is :770

summary: `getLocalConfig`'s non-1-exit rethrow (`src/git.ts:417`) is pinned by nothing — its only test block is win32-gated — while `isAncestor`'s identical arm is pinned; third body, so it files
acceptance: A case in `tests/git.test.ts` reaches `getLocalConfig`'s non-1-exit rethrow (`src/git.ts:417`) on every lane, not only win32: `pinLongPaths` (`src/git.ts:396`) is driven with `process.platform` reading `win32` — the shape `tests/spawnShim.test.ts:98` and `tests/setupWorktree.test.ts:36` already spell — over a cwd where `git config --local --get` exits something other than 1, and it rejects rather than resolving as unset. Parity with `isAncestor`'s own arm (`tests/git.test.ts:770`). Behavior-free: `src/git.ts` unchanged, `pnpm tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` green on both lanes.
pins: pinLongPaths rethrows a git config failure the probe cannot explain rather than reading it as unset
notes: Family *the config probe's non-1-exit rethrow has no pin, and the block it would live in runs on one host* — bodies `6a313c1d` (first) and `2cb1d145` (second, which said it queues on a third). This is the third. Re-verified on this tip: `:417` rethrows every code but 1, and `tests/git.test.ts:1861` is `describe.runIf(process.platform === "win32")`, the only block that reaches it. A `pins[]` and no `tests[]` — the property already holds; the pin is the whole work.
